notes: The bread/trap clause is compressed and difficult. Verses 12–14 use prohibitions; they may be heard as warnings or as reproach for actions already done. The draft retains their direct form.

The plural “you” who drank may be Judah or Edom, affecting the drinking image. The exile clause and Sepharad’s location are uncertain. Verse 21 follows the pointed active “deliverers,” not the alternative “those delivered.”
vocabulary: Ancestral names for Israel and Edom; “brother” makes Edom’s violence a betrayal of kinship.
Southern and lowland regions named as communities receiving territory in the restoration vision.
